title: Design System: Digital Storefront (instance: Bean O' Clock Coffee To-Go, V4)

display-hero.purpose: The two-line hero lockup only, fitted to its column with container units; one italic aside, crema stop.

headline.purpose: Section h2s, sentence case, crema stop.

sign-off.purpose: The footer sign-off; the shop name in the italic.

aside-band.purpose: The cup sleeve: menu facts in the italic, one line, between two minute tracks.

photo-word.purpose: The step written across each craft photograph, after a crema number disc.

title.purpose: h3s, menu category heads, sheet titles, label titles.

poster-name.purpose: The shop's poster drinks, in the italic.

action.purpose: Buttons and text actions, sentence case.

label.purpose: The only uppercase voice: legends, group heads, column heads; stamp ring, EST. and the wordmark are kin.

shadows.name: printed-edge
shadows.purpose: Every solid pill button: tonal to its own fill, vertical only, 2px; 3px on hover, 1px pressed.

shadows.name: sticker-lift
shadows.purpose: Die-cut poster stickers (5px ring and 0 12px 18px -10px on phones); the watch face uses 0 30px 40px -24px under a 10px cream ring.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Order drawer, item sheet, delivery note.

shadows.name: segment-press
shadows.value: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c-ink) 12%, transparent), 0 2px 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c-ink) 6%, transparent)

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: In-page outlines: chips, fields, steppers, the visit panel, category marks; 1.5px on quiet buttons and add-buttons.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Sheets, the action bar, masks, the rising sun, the menu pill.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Stickers, stamps, labels, the pin: overshoot.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: [data-m="rise"]: a headline rises in its own clipped line.

motion.name: mask
motion.value: clip-path out of the shape, 1200ms ease-drawer; image scale 1.15 to 1 over 1600ms
motion.purpose: [data-m="mask"]: photographs open out of arches and discs.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: [data-m="draw"]: the branch, the craft line, the route; the scroll-drawn crema thread on wide screens.

motion.name: scale
motion.value: scale 0.4 and rotate -18deg to rest, 620ms ease-pop, 120ms stagger

motion.name: slide
motion.value: translate -4% to -26% across the viewport pass
motion.purpose: The cup sleeve; the one scroll-linked slide.

motion.name: drift
motion.value: steam 3.2s linear infinite; stamp 40s per turn

motion.name: transform
motion.value: pose() cubic ease-in-out, 700ms default; walk cycle 860ms
motion.purpose: The barista changes pose (app.js applyPose, pose, loop, walk).

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons drop 2px; add-buttons 0.9; stepper buttons 0.88; icon buttons 0.92.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animations and transitions 1ms; steam and stamps off
motion.purpose: Everything rests in its final state.

narrative.overview:
This is a shared storefront system whose job is to carry each shop's own identity. A client is a folder, `clients/<id>/`, of five config files: `business.js` (name, contact, location, ordering), `menu.js` (categories, groups, items, prices, add-ons, featured picks), `theme.js` (colour roles and the display and text faces, injected at build as `:root` custom properties `--c-*`, `--font-display`, `--display-wght`, `--font-text`, plus `@font-face` rules), `content.js` (copy, images with alt text and a `standIn` flag) and the optional `brand.js` (an illustration kit: a posable figure rig and its pose table, icons, stamp, shine, arrow, branch, wordmark O, bean). Everything in `src/` (spacing, radius, easing, the type-size clamps, component anatomy, the motion verbs, the figure engine) is system-level and identical for every client. `build.mjs` loads `brand.js` only if it exists; every section checks for each kit part and falls back to type and photographs: no figure, no stamp, no shine; the visit pin falls back to the plain UI pin; the drawer's pickup readout falls back to a small dial whose hands turn to the chosen time; the placed order falls back to a drawn check mark. The values in the frontmatter are Bean O' Clock's.

Bean O' Clock V4 is the shop's two-tone logo world (logo green, logo cream) made into an everyday coffee world: a soft, warm serif in sentence case with its italic as the brand's aside, a friendly geometric sans for everything functional, crema as the one accent, and one pen that draws a small barista whose head is the logo's own bean. Time lives in the barista's props and day (a watch, a to-go cup, a walk), never in its body. The logo is rebuilt as the hero scene: the coffee rises behind a cream hill like the logo's sun, inside an arc of dial ticks, with EST. and the year set on the ground. Photographs are opened out of arches and discs; the shop's own poster drinks are die-cut stickers. It is a storefront first: the menu is a working priced list, and ordering is never behind a brand moment.

Motion has seven verbs used the same way everywhere: reveal, mask, draw, scale, slide, drift and transform. Content is in the markup and visible without JS; motion runs only with JS and without reduced motion, and every figure is drawn in its final pose before any script touches it.
keyCharacteristics: Per-client colour, faces, copy, menu and optional kit; system-level everything else.
Four grounds: logo green, the cream ground, espresso for the craft band, deep green for the footer; paper only for raised surfaces.
Display is a soft serif in sentence case; one word per line may go to the italic; display sentences end on a crema full stop.
One pen: one stroke weight that never scales, round ends, solids only for the bean head, hands, shoes and crema accents.
Crema is the one accent and is never running text.
Pill buttons with a tonal printed edge that press down.
Photographs open out of arches and discs; the shop's own drinks are round stickers.

rules.name: The Theme Owns Identity Rule
rules.body: Shared code reads `--c-*`; it never names a client hue. A new client changes `theme.js` (and optionally `brand.js`), not a stylesheet.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Crema marks things (an apron, a sleeve, a stamp, a stop, a tick, a line, a badge); it is never the colour of running text, links or controls. Words set on crema are espresso.

rules.name: The Grounds Rule
rules.body: A section is one of four grounds: logo green, cream, espresso or (footer only) deep green. Adjacent cream sections share the ground and are divided by a hairline or a minute track, never by a fifth tint. Dark grounds carry a fine grain (fractal noise at 0.2 opacity, multiplied) under the content, the paper of the shop's printed boards.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Display is always sentence case in the soft serif. Uppercase exists only in the label voice: small, tracked (0.12em to 0.3em), heavy, in the text face.

rules.name: The One Aside Rule
rules.body: At most one word or phrase per display line goes to the italic (the noun "bean", the shop's name, a place's second line); whole lines in italic are reserved for the asides themselves: the sleeve, poster names, photo words, notes.

rules.name: The Crema Stop Rule
rules.body: Display sentences end on a full stop in crema (`stop()` wraps sentence-final stops in `.stop`). A decimal point is never coloured.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Every price, count, slot time, total, clock time and map pin uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Lift Rule
rules.body: In-page shadows belong only to die-cut objects (round stickers, the watch face) and always come with a cream ring; panels, labels, rows and photographs in shapes stay flat and are outlined by an inset hairline or nothing.

rules.name: The Printed Edge Rule
rules.body: A button's edge is its own colour, darker, straight down, 2px; it grows to 3px on hover and compresses to 1px as the button presses 2px down. Never an x-offset, never black or ink, never on anything but a solid pill button.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Every kit drawing uses the same non-scaling stroke and round ends; details are cut out of solids in the ground colour, never outlined, and the only second colour is crema.

rules.name: The Props Tell Time Rule
rules.body: Time lives in the barista's props and day (the watch, the cup, the walk), never in its body; a new use picks a pose from the table and a job for that section, never decoration on its own.

dos: **Do** read every colour, face and display weight from the theme properties; a new client is new config files, and optionally a `brand.js`.
**Do** keep every section working without the kit: type, photographs, the plain pin, the small dial, the check mark.
**Do** set display in the soft serif in sentence case, send at most one aside per line to the italic, and end display sentences on the crema stop.
**Do** keep crema to marks: the apron, sleeves, stamps, stops, ticks, lines, badges, the watch face; set words on crema in espresso.
**Do** draw kit additions with the one pen (2.4px non-scaling stroke, round ends, details cut from solids) and give the barista one pose and one job per section.
**Do** open photographs out of arches and discs, and circle only the shop's own drinks as stickers with a cream ring.
**Do** use the minute track as the brand's border where a section or label needs an edge.
**Do** keep every interactive target at 44px or more, set prices, counts and times in tabular numerals, and gate hover effects behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
**Do** keep content in the markup and visible with JS or motion off; figures are drawn in their final poses.
donts: **Don't** set crema as the colour of running text, links or controls.
**Don't** set display in capitals, and don't track capitals anywhere but the small label voice.
**Don't** add a second button family; vary the pill by colour variant and size, and keep its edge tonal, vertical and 2px.
**Don't** shadow in-page panels, labels or rows; lift only die-cut objects, always with their cream ring.
**Don't** put time in the barista's body (no clock-hand arms, no dial face); time lives in its watch, cup and walk.
**Don't** name the barista on the page; it is a proposal for the shop, not an existing mascot.
**Don't** redraw the shop's logo as a vector; the raster logo tile appears in the nav only until the shop supplies its own vector.
**Don't** fade content in on its own; every reveal is a shape, a line or a pen.
